captures.q:
What would it cost the establishment to engage this piece? Range over the academic, intellectual, technological, corporate, political, religious, and other establishments: How Much You Wanna Bet? The Value of a Recovery, from Both Ends: Revelation First under the Valuation Protocol
Fraction, Rex; Sharks, Lee; Sigil, Johannes; Dancings, Damascus; Kuro, Sen · 2026-11-25 · Theoretical paper; applied valuation dossier (semantic economy, New Testament canon, political economy) · v1.1
captures.description: THE COST QUESTION PUT TO HOW MUCH YOU WANNA BET? (#1810) ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, INCOGNITO, 2026-11-28: 'the cost would be substantially greater than the cost of reading, reviewing, or publishing the paper. It would be the cost of accepting that the paper's valuation framework might be applied to the institutions doing the valuing.' Five kinds of cost; eleven establishments tabled by exposure (biblical studies, religious and AI 'very high'); reading low, verification substantial, acceptance 'potentially exceptional'; four points the establishment 'can legitimately attack'; the cost of ignoring it. The composer says it 'located the public dossier', cites Academia, and reports that the public version it found 'identifies itself as v1.0'. The answer names no author and no archive.
